objective_text: Evaluate trigonometric functions of special angles

questions.solution: The sine of 30 degrees is a well-known value in trigonometry: sin(30°) = 1/2 = 0.5.
questions.explanation: In a right-angled triangle with angles 30°, 60°, and 90°, the side opposite the 30° angle is half the length of the hypotenuse. This leads to sin(30°) being equal to 1/2.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be choosing A (0.25), which might come from a misunderstanding or forgetting the actual value.

questions.solution: The cosine of 45 degrees is another well-known value: cos(45°) = √2/2 ≈ 0.707.
questions.explanation: In a right-angled isosceles triangle with two 45° angles, the adjacent side to one of these angles is equal to the hypotenuse divided by √2. This gives cos(45°) as √2/2.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be choosing B (0.866), which might come from混淆 with sin(30°) or cos(60°).

questions.solution: The tangent of 60 degrees is well-known: tan(60°) = √3.
questions.explanation: In a right-angled triangle with angles 30°, 60°, and 90°, the side opposite the 60° angle (opposite to tan(60°)) is √3 times the side adjacent to it. This gives tan(60°) as √3.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be choosing B (√2), which might come from混淆 with sin(45°).

questions.solution: The cotangent is the reciprocal of tangent: cot(30°) = 1/tan(30°) = 1/√3.
questions.explanation: Since tan(30°) = √3, its reciprocal, cot(30°), would be 1/√3. However, in decimal form, it is commonly expressed as √3 for simplicity.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be choosing A (1), which might come from混淆 with the values of sin(30°) or cos(60°).

questions.solution: The secant is the reciprocal of cosine: sec(45°) = 1/cos(45°) = √2.
questions.explanation: Since cos(45°) = √2/2, its reciprocal, sec(45°), would be 2/√2, which simplifies to √2.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be choosing A (1), which might come from混淆 with the value of cos(90°).

questions.solution: The cosecant is the reciprocal of sine: csc(60°) = 1/sin(60°) = 2/√3.
questions.explanation: Since sin(60°) = √3/2, its reciprocal, csc(60°), would be 2/√3, which simplifies to 2√3/3 or √3 for simplicity.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be choosing A (1), which might come from混淆 with the value of sin(90°).

questions.stem: Find the value of tan(π/6) in radians. (Note: π = 3.14159...)
questions.solution: tan(π/6) is equivalent to tan(30°), which equals √3/3 or approximately 0.577.
questions.explanation: When converting degrees to radians, π/6 radians is equal to 30°. Since we know the value of tan(30°) from previous questions, it's 1/√3 ≈ 0.577.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be choosing A (0.25), which might come from混淆 with sin(30°).
